source.notes: CISCE item bank 'ISC Competency-Focused Practice Questions', Chemistry, ISC-Class XII. The preface (PDF page 2) is dated July 2024 and signed by the Chief Executive & Secretary, CISCE; it says competency-focused questions are part of ICSE/ISC examinations from 2024, and that the Answer Key 'presents the possible answers to a given question, but it is neither limiting nor exhaustive'. No examination year, paper code, maximum marks or duration is printed. The file is 49 PDF pages: page 1 blank, page 2 preface, page 3 table of contents, pages 4-33 questions (printed pages 1-30), pages 34-48 'ANSWER KEY' (printed pages 31-45), page 49 blank. answerSourceUrl is the same PDF. 97 questions in six sections, marks from the section headings: I Multiple Choice Questions (1-23, 1 Mark Each), II Assertion-Reason (24-28, 1 Mark Each), III Fill in the Blanks (29-38, 1 Mark Each), IV Very Short Answer (39-62, 2 Marks Each), V Short Answer (63-92, 3 Marks Each), VI Long Answer (93-97, 5 Marks Each); total 201 marks (not a paper, so no maximum). Each question prints a topic in square brackets (used for the chapter suggestion; 'Block Elements' is mapped to d-and-f-block-elements) and a cognitive tag in brackets, recorded as cognitiveLevel as printed (e.g. 'Evaluate & Analysis'); questions 89 and 90 print separate tags per sub-part and have no single cognitiveLevel. Sub-parts (a)/(b)/(c) are kept together in one entry because marks are only given per question. In the text layer questions 27/28 and 29-38 (and answers 43/44) are laid out out of order; they were matched to their numbers using the rendered pages. Chemical subscripts, superscripts and ionic charges print flat in the text layer; they were rebuilt as Unicode sub/superscripts only where pdfplumber character sizes and the rendered page confirm them (flagged per question, confidence MEDIUM). Where the page itself prints a formula flat (e.g. '[Co(en)3]3+' in Q40, 'CoCl3.6NH3' in Q94) it is kept flat. Letter subscripts (Kb, Kf, ∆Tf) are written inline. Typos are kept as printed (e.g. 'Enzaldehyde' in Q52). Figures, graphs, structure images and reaction schemes are not reproduced; where an official answer is only a drawing, the answer entry ends at the part label and is flagged.

questions.text:
Give reason:
(a) d-block elements exhibit larger number of oxidation state than f-block elements.
(b) Increase in atomic number does not change atomic radii among the transition elements.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) d- block elements exhibit more oxidation states as the energy gap is comparable and not much, while in f-block elements the energy gap between f and d subshell is comparatively higher.
(b)With increase in atomic number in transition series, the nuclear charge increases which tends to decrease the size but addition of electron in d-subshell increases the screening effect. Therefore, the increased nuclear charge is partly balanced and hence, the atomic radii does not change much.

questions.text: Halides of transition elements in higher oxidation states are more covalent. Give reason.

officialAnswer.text: This is because in higher oxidation states the size of the metal ion decreases/more vacant d-orbitals are available for bonding. Electronegativity difference between the transition metal and the halogen tends to decrease. This results in more equal sharing of electrons between the metal and the halogen.
